summary: Environment A direct-binary verification for the Phase 8 Windows rebuild (Production Integration - OBS/vMix text push) - this phase adds two new Rust crates and new orchestration code compiled into the desktop binary, so a genuine rebuild with direct binary proof is required.
buildResult: Rust build succeeded (whisper-rs-sys ggml lib-name two-pass fix applied as expected on the first-attempt failure, unrelated to this phase's own changes - cip-integrations-obs and cip-integrations-vmix both compiled cleanly on the first pass alongside it); pnpm build (tsc -b && vite build) succeeded producing a fresh dist/assets bundle; NSIS packaging finished with the three runtime DLLs confirmed present by the script's own built-in check.

installer.fileSizeDeltaNote: A real increase, consistent with two new crates (cip-integrations-obs, cip-integrations-vmix) and their new dependencies (tungstenite, ureq, sha2, base64) compiled into the binary, plus the new production.rs orchestration module and four new commands - the installer's SHA-256 changing, plus the newSymbolsThisPhase entries below, are the decisive proof this rebuild reflects this phase's real code.

extractionMethod: 7z x against the built installer into a scratch directory; confirmed exit code 0 and listed contents.

symbolRegressionCheck.method: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings/nm against the extracted cip-desktop.exe, re-run for every prior-phase symbol/string this project has established as a regression tripwire.

whisper_full_with_state.note: Stable at 96 for a second consecutive rebuild since the Phase 7.3 investigation confirmed this is the same non-deterministic strings/grep line-coalescing artifact previously stabilized at 93 for nine rebuilds (Phase 6.2-7.2) - no file in ai/speech, integrations/audio, or any whisper-rs-touching path changed this phase either.

symbolRegressionCheck.conclusion: Every prior-phase Rust-side symbol/string count is exactly unchanged from the Phase 7.3 baseline. Zero regression in any pre-existing feature.

newSymbolsThisPhase.method: x86_64-w64-mingw32-nm -C against the extracted cip-desktop.exe, searching for this phase's own new function names - direct proof the real production-integration code actually compiled into this exact binary.
newSymbolsThisPhase.workerThreadProof: core::ptr::drop_in_place<std::thread::lifecycle::spawn_unchecked<cip_desktop_lib::production::push_to_configured_targets::{{closure}},()>::{{closure}}> is present - direct proof the worker-thread dispatch (not just the function definitions) is genuinely compiled into this exact binary, matching the acoustic/speech worker precedent this phase's design deliberately mirrors.
newSymbolsThisPhase.conclusion: All 8 expected new symbols present with real, distinct addresses, plus direct evidence of the worker-thread dispatch itself - direct proof this phase's implementation is compiled into this exact packaged .exe.

frontendTextSearch.conclusion: Reproduces the established Tauri-frontend-bundle tooling limitation (documented since Phase 6.1) an eleventh time for UI copy specifically - the control string itself returns 0 matches, so this says nothing about correctness either way. The command-name string itself (used by both the Rust #[tauri::command] registration and the frontend's invoke() call) does appear, at the same count (2) as every other single-command name in this codebase's symbol table. Correctness for the frontend surface rests on npm run typecheck's success, the fresh Vite build producing a new asset bundle hash, and the full 266/266 frontend test pass already recorded in pilot-evidence/8/build/production-integration-evidence.json.

architecturalSafetyNotes: Exactly four new Tauri commands, zero new events, zero new database schema.
core/presentation and core/music (domain contract crates) have zero symbol-level changes.
Every prior acoustic-recognition and presentation-router symbol tracked above is present and unchanged - confirmed by direct nm lookup, not just absence of a regression flag.

New dependencies (tungstenite, ureq, sha2, base64) verified pure-Rust with no TLS backend via cargo tree before this rebuild - re-confirmed by this build's own compile log showing no rustls/ring/webpki-roots crates compiled.
environmentCStatus: NOT YET VERIFIED for this exact artifact - the decisive pending gate is the operator's own real-hardware test: with real OBS and/or vMix running, configure a target in the Production Integration panel, click Test Connection and confirm the named source/input updates, then Save and confirm displaying a real verse/slide in CIP updates that same source/input live, and that clearing the display blanks it.
